chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about something from the expiation for an oath, so he said: 'He should fast for three days.' I said, 'He is weak from fasting and is unable (to do it).' He said: 'He should give charity to ten poor people.' I said, 'He is unable to do that.' He said: 'So let him seek forgiveness of Allah and not repeat it, for it is the best of the expiations, and its maximum and its minimum. So let him seek forgiveness of his Lord and display repentance and remorse.'
ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for breaking an oath if one cannot fast or feed the poor?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes a graded hierarchy for expiating broken oaths, culminating in istighfar (seeking forgiveness) as both the minimum and maximum penalty for those unable to fast or feed the poor. Shia scholars highlight the unique designation of istighfar as the 'best' expiation, emphasizing that sincere repentance (tawbah) with remorse (nadamah) holds profound spiritual weight, potentially surpassing material acts like feeding the needy in terms of divine acceptance.
